knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Zhang_2026_tacrolimus")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S620915>

Zhang and colleagues built a one-compartment population PK model for oral
tacrolimus from routine trough concentrations in 22 Chinese adults with
connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD).
Only body weight was retained, through fixed allometric exponents.
Posaconazole lowered the objective function significantly but was left out
because the effect rested on a single patient with two concentrations. The
model was then used in a Monte Carlo simulation to propose a starting dose of
0.10 mg/kg/day (in two doses) for adults of 50-100 kg, targeting a trough of
5-10 ng/mL.

# Population

The analysis used 22 adults with CTD-ILD treated at a single centre
(Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University, Jiangsu, China) between
August 2022 and September 2025: 17 with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, 3
with Sjogren syndrome and 2 with undifferentiated connective tissue disease.
Baseline characteristics (Table 1 of the source) were: 6 men / 16 women; age
mean 59.29 years (SD 10.23), range 42-75; body weight mean 66.07 kg
(SD 8.94), median 66.50, range 47.5-93. Concomitant medication counts are
Table 2; prednisone (14/22) and co-trimoxazole (12/22) were the most common.

The 31 observations (1-3 per patient) are all troughs taken before the next
dose, assayed by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay (Emit 2000; routine range
2-30 ng/mL, LLOQ 2 ng/mL). The single value below the LLOQ (1.6 ng/mL) was
kept as reported. The paper reports no administered doses.

```{r population}
str(ui$population, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F at 70 kg) | 20.3 L/h | Table 3 and Equation (8); RSE 12.7%, bootstrap median 18.9 [12.2, 24.2] |
| `lvc` (V/F at 70 kg) | 1920 L | Table 3 and Equation (9); RSE 35.3%, bootstrap median 1905 [990, 6639] |
| `lka` (absorption rate constant) | 4.48 1/h, **fixed** | Table 3 "4.48 (fixed)"; Methods, Modeling, citing references 32-34 |
| `e_wt_cl` (allometric exponent, CL/F) | 0.75, **fixed** | Methods, Equation (5), citing Anderson & Holford 2008; Equation (8) |
| `e_wt_vc` (allometric exponent, V/F) | 1, **fixed** | Methods, Equation (5); Equation (9) |
| `etalcl` (IIV on CL/F) | 0.480 as an **SD** (variance 0.2304) | Table 3 (omega_CL/F, RSE 20.8%); bootstrap median 0.447 [0.092, 0.617]; scale settled in Check 2 |
| `propSd` (proportional residual error) | 0.346 | Table 3 (sigma1, "proportional error"); bootstrap median 0.339 [0.073, 0.516] |
| `addSd` (additive residual error) | 0.322 ng/mL | Table 3 (sigma2, "additive error"); bootstrap median 0.411 [0.010, 1.456] |
| Structural model: 1-compartment, first-order oral absorption | n/a | Methods, Modeling (CL/F, V/F and Ka) |
| IIV form `A_i = TV(A) * exp(eta_i)` | n/a | Methods, Equation (1) |
| Residual form `B_i = C_i + C_i * eps_1 + eps_2` | n/a | Methods, Equation (4); Table 3 lists both sigma1 and sigma2 |
| Reference weight 70 kg | n/a | Methods, Equation (5) |
| Simulation regimen: daily dose split evenly into two doses; target 5-10 ng/mL | n/a | Methods, Simulation |

The nine equations are images in the article; the values above were read
from the typeset equations and cross-checked against Table 3.

# Simulation design

The paper's Methods state that every simulated daily dose (0.01-0.14
mg/kg/day) "was split evenly into twice a day", in six weight groups of
50-100 kg, but not when the simulated trough was read. With a typical
half-life of about 66 h (V/F 1920 L, CL/F 20.3 L/h) steady state takes more
than two weeks, so the answer matters: a steady-state trough at
0.10 mg/kg/day averages about 14 ng/mL, well above the published centre of
about 7 ng/mL in Figure 4. Check 2 shows that the published curves are
reproduced by the trough **12 h after the sixth dose** (72 h, just before the
morning dose of day 4), which fits the paper's focus on the *initial* dose.

Because the model has a single random effect (`etalcl`), the between-subject
distribution is represented by a deterministic lattice of 200 equally spaced
normal quantiles rather than by random draws, so every number in this
vignette is identical on every machine. The model is linear, so each weight
is solved once at 1 mg/kg/day and the troughs are scaled by the dose. One
solve gives troughs after several dose counts, read 0.01 h before each
scheduled dose so the sample does not include the dose given at that time.

```{r cohort}
n_lattice <- 200L
omega_sd <- 0.480 # Table 3, read as a standard deviation (see Check 2)
z_grid <- stats::qnorm((seq_len(n_lattice) - 0.5) / n_lattice)

weights <- c(50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100)
doses <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10, 0.12, 0.14) # mg/kg/day
n_doses_candidates <- c(4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 14L, 80L)
n_doses_used <- 6L
trough_time <- function(n) 12 * n - 0.01

make_events <- function(wt, w_index) {
  ids <- (w_index - 1L) * n_lattice + seq_len(n_lattice)
  dose <- tibble::tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = wt * 1 / 2, ii = 12,
    addl = max(n_doses_candidates) - 1L, cmt = "depot"
  )
  # Observations on the ODE state `central`; Cc is returned alongside it.
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, n_doses = n_doses_candidates) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = trough_time(n_doses), evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, ii = 0,
      addl = 0L, cmt = "central"
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-n_doses)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt, etalcl = z_grid[match(id, ids)] * omega_sd)
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(weights), function(i) {
  make_events(weights[i], i)
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(events$id) == length(weights) * n_lattice)
```

```{r simulate}
sim1 <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame"
))
tr_all <- sim1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_doses = round((time + 0.01) / 12)) |>
  dplyr::filter(n_doses %in% n_doses_candidates) |>
  dplyr::select(id, WT, cl, n_doses, trough_per_mgkgday = Cc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(z = z_grid[((id - 1L) %% n_lattice) + 1L])
stopifnot(
  nrow(tr_all) == length(weights) * n_lattice * length(n_doses_candidates),
  !anyNA(tr_all$trough_per_mgkgday)
)

troughs <- tr_all |>
  dplyr::filter(n_doses == n_doses_used) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(dose = doses) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = trough_per_mgkgday * dose)
```

# Check 1 -- target attainment (Figure 5)

The paper's primary endpoint is the probability that the trough lies in the
5-10 ng/mL target window, plotted against weight for each dose in Figure 5.
The published probabilities below were read from that figure by the
maintainers (precision about 1 percentage point); the paper simulated 1,000
patients per scenario, so its own Monte Carlo error is about 1-1.5 points.
The 0.01, 0.02 and 0.04 mg/kg/day curves lie on zero.

```{r published-pta}
# Rows: dose (mg/kg/day); columns: body weight (kg). Read from Figure 5.
fig5 <- rbind(
  `0.01` = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  `0.02` = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  `0.04` = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  `0.06` = c(13.2, 15.8, 17.4, 18.8, 20.2, 22.2),
  `0.08` = c(68.5, 72.3, 74.8, 77.3, 78.6, 80.0),
  `0.1` = c(89.1, 90.9, 92.3, 92.9, 93.6, 93.5),
  `0.12` = c(83.3, 81.2, 80.2, 79.2, 78.5, 76.5),
  `0.14` = c(54.1, 51.0, 48.2, 45.8, 42.6, 41.3)
)
colnames(fig5) <- weights
published <- as.data.frame(as.table(fig5), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::transmute(dose = as.numeric(Var1), WT = as.numeric(Var2), pta_published = Freq)
```

```{r pta}
in_window <- function(c) mean(c >= 5 & c <= 10)

pta <- troughs |>
  dplyr::group_by(WT, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta_model = 100 * in_window(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published, by = c("WT", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = pta_model - pta_published)

pta |>
  dplyr::select(dose, WT, pta_model) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose = sprintf("%.2f", dose)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = WT, values_from = pta_model) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg/day)" = dose) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Model probability (%) of a 5-10 ng/mL trough after six doses, by body weight (kg).")

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Statistic = c("Median abs. difference", "90th percentile abs. difference", "Max abs. difference"),
    `Percentage points` = c(
      stats::median(abs(pta$diff)),
      stats::quantile(abs(pta$diff), 0.9),
      max(abs(pta$diff))
    )
  ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Model vs published target attainment over all 48 dose-weight cells of Figure 5."
)
```

```{r pta-gate}
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL/F, V/F, exponent or regimen moves the
  # curves by tens of points.
  stats::median(abs(pta$diff)) < 1.5,
  # Envelope: published values are digitised and carry Monte Carlo error.
  stats::quantile(abs(pta$diff), 0.9) < 3,
  max(abs(pta$diff)) < 5
)
```

```{r figure-5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Zhang 2026: probability of a 5-10 ng/mL trough after six doses. Lines: model; points: values read from the published figure."}
pta |>
  ggplot(aes(WT, pta_model, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = pta_published), shape = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "Probability of 5-10 ng/mL (%)",
    colour = "Dose (mg/kg/day)"
  )
```

# Check 2 -- trough timing and which quantities are on which scale

Table 3 prints `omega_CL/F = 0.480`, `sigma1 = 0.346` and `sigma2 = 0.322`
without saying whether they are standard deviations or variances, the paper
does not say whether its Monte Carlo included residual error, and it does not
say when the trough was read. Each combination makes a different prediction,
so they are compared against Figure 5. Residual error is added analytically
(normal error with variance `addSd^2 + (propSd * C)^2`), keeping the
comparison deterministic.

```{r scale-check}
prop_sd <- ui$theta[["propSd"]]
add_sd <- ui$theta[["addSd"]]

pta_variant <- function(n_doses, omega_scale, prop, add) {
  tr_all |>
    dplyr::filter(n_doses == !!n_doses) |>
    dplyr::mutate(c1 = trough_per_mgkgday * exp(z * (omega_scale - omega_sd))) |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(dose = doses) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Cc_v = c1 * dose, sd_v = sqrt(add^2 + (prop * Cc_v)^2)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(WT, dose) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      pta = if (prop == 0 && add == 0) {
        100 * in_window(Cc_v)
      } else {
        100 * mean(stats::pnorm((10 - Cc_v) / sd_v) - stats::pnorm((5 - Cc_v) / sd_v))
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(published, by = c("WT", "dose")) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      median_abs = stats::median(abs(pta - pta_published)),
      max_abs = max(abs(pta - pta_published))
    )
}

variants <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    reading = sprintf("omega SD, no residual error, trough after %d doses", n_doses_candidates),
    n_doses = n_doses_candidates, omega_scale = omega_sd, prop = 0, add = 0
  ),
  tibble::tribble(
    ~reading, ~n_doses, ~omega_scale, ~prop, ~add,
    "omega variance (SD 0.693), no residual error, 6 doses", 6L, sqrt(0.480), 0, 0,
    "omega SD, residual SDs included, 6 doses", 6L, 0.480, prop_sd, add_sd,
    "omega variance, residual variances included, 6 doses", 6L, sqrt(0.480), sqrt(prop_sd), sqrt(add_sd)
  )
)
variants <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  variants,
  dplyr::bind_rows(Map(pta_variant, variants$n_doses, variants$omega_scale, variants$prop, variants$add))
)

variants |>
  dplyr::select(reading, median_abs, max_abs) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Reading" = reading, "Median abs. difference (points)" = median_abs,
    "Max abs. difference (points)" = max_abs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Agreement with Figure 5 under each reading of Table 3 and each trough time. The last candidate (80 doses, 40 days) is effectively steady state.")

packaged <- variants$n_doses == n_doses_used & variants$omega_scale == omega_sd & variants$prop == 0
stopifnot(
  sum(packaged) == 1,
  variants$median_abs[packaged] < 1.5,
  all(variants$median_abs[!packaged] > 3 * variants$median_abs[packaged])
)
```

Only one combination reproduces the paper: `omega_CL/F` a standard deviation,
probabilities computed on individual predictions without residual error, and
the trough read 12 h after the sixth dose. One dose more or fewer misses by
7-9 points on average and by up to 26-33 points in a single cell, and
steady-state troughs miss by nearly 40 points on average. Reading the omega
as a variance widens the distribution enough to miss by about 8 points on
average, and adding the residual error misses by about 10. (The medians
include the 18 cells at 0.01-0.04 mg/kg/day, where every reading gives
zero.) This check settles the omega scale only: residual error is absent
from the paper's simulations, so the figure says nothing about whether
`sigma1` and `sigma2` are SDs or variances. They are packaged as SDs, the
convention the same group's Table 3 format follows (compare
`Wang_2019b_tacrolimus`).

# Check 3 -- Table 4 recommended dose

```{r table4}
t4 <- troughs |>
  dplyr::filter(dose == 0.10) |>
  dplyr::group_by(WT) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    in_window = 100 * in_window(Cc),
    below_5 = 100 * mean(Cc < 5),
    above_10 = 100 * mean(Cc > 10),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Probability 5-10 ng/mL (%)", "Probability below 5 ng/mL (%)", "Probability above 10 ng/mL (%)"),
  Published = c("89.1-93.5", "6.3-10.9", "0-0.2"),
  Model = c(
    sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(t4$in_window), max(t4$in_window)),
    sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(t4$below_5), max(t4$below_5)),
    sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(t4$above_10), max(t4$above_10))
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 4 of Zhang 2026: 0.10 mg/kg/day across 50-100 kg.")

stopifnot(
  abs(min(t4$in_window) - 89.1) < 3,
  abs(max(t4$in_window) - 93.5) < 3,
  max(t4$above_10) < 2
)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Zhang 2026: simulated troughs after six doses by dose and weight. Dashed lines: 5-10 ng/mL target."}
troughs |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(dose), Cc)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(5, 10), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(WT, "kg"), ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Daily dose (mg/kg/day, in two doses)", y = "Trough (ng/mL)")
```

The published Figure 4 clouds have a sharp upper edge at roughly 100 times
the daily dose in mg/kg (10 ng/mL at 0.10 mg/kg/day). That edge is the
accumulated dose over volume for a subject with very low clearance: six half
doses of 0.05 mg/kg each into 1920 L per 70 kg give at most
6 x 0.05 x 70 / 1920 x 1000 = 10.9 ng/mL. The model shows the same
bounded upper tail.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no non-compartmental analysis, so `ncaComparisonTable()` is
not used. Instead PKNCA is run on a single 5 mg oral dose to a 70 kg lattice
and compared with the model's closed-form solution. Both sides use the same
parameters, so the difference is purely numerical and the bound is tight.

```{r pknca}
nca_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3, by = 0.02), seq(3.5, 24, by = 0.5), seq(26, 480, by = 2))))
nca_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    id = seq_len(n_lattice), time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 5, cmt = "depot"
  ),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_lattice), time = nca_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 70, etalcl = z_grid[id] * omega_sd, treatment = "5 mg single oral dose") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

nca_sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = nca_events, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = "treatment"
))

sim_nca <- nca_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

dose_df <- nca_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

nca_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
    aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(nca_data)
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r pknca-vs-closed-form}
closed_form <- nca_sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl, vc, ka) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    kel = cl / vc,
    aucinf_cf = 1000 * 5 / cl,
    halflife_cf = log(2) / kel,
    tmax_cf = log(ka / kel) / (ka - kel)
  )

cmp <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "tmax")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(closed_form, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (aucinf.obs - aucinf_cf) / aucinf_cf,
    hl_pct = 100 * (half.life - halflife_cf) / halflife_cf,
    tmax_pct = 100 * (tmax - tmax_cf) / tmax_cf
  )

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Parameter = c("AUC0-inf vs Dose/(CL/F)", "Half-life vs ln(2)/kel", "Tmax vs ln(ka/kel)/(ka-kel)"),
    `Median % difference` = c(stats::median(cmp$auc_pct), stats::median(cmp$hl_pct), stats::median(cmp$tmax_pct)),
    `Max abs % difference` = c(max(abs(cmp$auc_pct)), max(abs(cmp$hl_pct)), max(abs(cmp$tmax_pct)))
  ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "PKNCA on the simulation vs the model's own closed-form solution."
)

# Same parameters on both sides: differences are numerical only. Tmax is
# resolved to half a 0.02 h grid step (under 1% of the ~1.3 h Tmax).
stopifnot(
  max(abs(cmp$auc_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(cmp$hl_pct)) < 1,
  max(abs(cmp$tmax_pct)) < 2
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **`omega_CL/F = 0.480` is read as a standard deviation** (about 50% CV;
  see Check 2): the variance reading cannot reproduce Figure 5.
- **`sigma1 = 0.346` and `sigma2 = 0.322 ng/mL` are read as SDs** of the
  proportional and additive components of Equation (4). The paper's dosing
  simulations do not use them, so nothing in the paper tests this reading;
  it follows the convention of the same group's earlier tacrolimus model
  (`Wang_2019b_tacrolimus`). `sigma2` is poorly determined (RSE 100.5%,
  bootstrap bias +27.6%).
- **Published attainment excludes residual error.** The paper does not say
  so, but only the individual-prediction calculation reproduces Figure 5
  (Check 2).
- **Trough time in the simulations.** The paper does not state it. Reading the
  trough 12 h after the sixth dose (72 h) reproduces Figure 5; earlier, later
  and steady-state troughs do not (Check 2). This concerns only how the
  vignette replicates the paper's figure; the packaged model is unaffected.
  Note that tacrolimus is far from steady state at that point with these
  parameters (typical half-life about 66 h), so the paper's 0.10 mg/kg/day
  recommendation targets the day-4 trough, and a typical patient continuing
  that dose would accumulate to a steady-state trough of about 14 ng/mL.
- **V/F is poorly determined.** The bootstrap 95% interval is 990-6639 L
  (Table 3), and the authors note that sparse troughs carry little
  information on V/F. Because the half-life depends on V/F, so do the early
  troughs the paper's simulations rely on.
- **Posaconazole.** Its effect on CL/F was significant (Table S1) but the
  authors did not report its size and excluded it from the final model; the
  packaged model has no posaconazole effect and should not be used to predict
  that interaction.
- **Matrix.** The paper names the assay (Emit 2000 Tacrolimus, a whole-blood
  immunoassay) but not the matrix; the central compartment is recorded as
  whole blood on that basis.
- **Fixed `ka`.** 4.48 1/h is carried from the source's references 32-34
  (Wang 2020, two Xenobiotica tacrolimus analyses, and Cai 2020), as also
  used by `Wang_2019b_tacrolimus`.
- **Figure values were digitised by eye** from Figure 5 to about 1 percentage
  point. The gate is set on the median and 90th percentile of the absolute
  differences, not on individual cells.
